newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian buyers see corn, at two-year low, down more.
newsitem.headline: Asian buyers see corn, at two-year low, down more.

text.p: Buying interest returned to the Asian corn market on Thursday after Chicago futures prices dropped to the lowest levels in more than two years overnight and more losses were expected, dealers said.
"The corn (futures) must find a new support level and many buyers are waiting for it to bottom out," one trader said.

At the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), corn for July delivery touched a low of $2.55-3/4 a bushel, the lowest level for the nearby contract since May 1995. July closed four cents down on the day at $2.56-1/4.
"There are some corn buying and price inquiries going on today, particularly from Philippine and South Korea buyers," one trader said.
South Korea's KFPC placed a tender on Thursday for 50,000 tonnes of corn, while other Korean buyers were reported to be testing prices in the market.
"I think Korean buyers believed that the corn prices are fair right now so they started to buy some of their basic supplies," he added.
Southeast Asian corn buyers remained mainly sidelined on Thursday, however, as they generally expect further falls.
U.S. corn coming into Southeast Asia was seen by the trade at around $134-$136 a tonne C&F for August to September Panamax-size shipments against $136-$138 a week ago.
Chinese corn in Southeast Asia was quoted at between $132-$134 a tonne C&F for July/August shipment mainly on a Handy against $137-$139 last week.
Argentine corn is out of season, but was indicated at about $132 a tonne C&F for Panamax-size August shipment.
The soymeal market was also active on Thursday as South Korea's KFA placed a tender for between 30,000 to 35,000 tonnes of U.S. or Chinese soymeal, traders said.
They said the South Korean buying may lure Southeast Asian buyers into the soymeal market.
Dealers said Indonesia and Malaysia buyers are waiting for lower prices to buy up to 110,000 tonnes of soymeal.
"They are still waiting, because time is on their side," a dealer said.
Traders estimate that Indonesia buyers may purchase 50,000 to 90,000 tonnes of soymeal, while Malaysia buyers may buy 20,000 tonnes both for August and September deliveries.
They said there was also are some soymeal price inquiries from Thailand on Thursday, but no any concrete buying interest. -- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
